Marissa — quick check from my side: Google Calendar is interpreting the attached ICS as floating (no VTIMEZONE). When an ICS lacks proper timezone blocks, the client will apply the event time to the recipient's default zone which explains the 17:00 CEST display (Novus exported as 09:00 without TZ meta).

This is made worse by recent DST differences: US moved to DST two weeks ago while some EU systems handled VTIMEZONE differently, so an exported event without VTIMEZONE can end up an hour off.

I ran a quick test importing the attached Novus_Demo_Invite.ics into a fresh calendar — it showed as 09:00 local time, not 09:00 America/Los_Angeles.

Options: 
- Ask Sophie to resend with explicit timezone (VTIMEZONE/TZID) — preferred;
- We can propose an explicit slot in UTC to avoid ambiguity (e.g., 2026-05-21 16:00 UTC = 09:00 PDT / 18:00 CEST);
- Or accept a new slot from Novus.

I've attached a tiny CSV of our team's available windows to this thread (proposed-times.csv). If we want to be proactive, we can offer two alternatives: 2026-05-22 16:00 CEST (07:00 PDT) or 2026-05-22 11:00 CEST (02:00 PDT) — I know early for the US folks but might be workable.

-Jordan
